Apple rarely introduces entirely new screen sizes for the iPhone, but the iPhone Ultra arriving this autumn will come in two screen formats and sizes that have never before appeared on an iPhone. Here's what you can expect.

The iPhone Ultra will introduce two brand-new screen formats and sizes

For many years, the screen size options offered by the Apple iPhone lineup have been largely the same.

Occasional tweaks aside, recent iPhones have mainly split into two size categories: a 6.1- to 6.3-inch version, and a larger 6.7- to 6.9-inch version.

However, this year the iPhone Ultra will bring two entirely new screen sizes that are different from anything we've seen before.

The rumored screen sizes for the iPhone Ultra are as follows:

  • Around a 5.3-inch outer screen
  • Around a 7.6-inch inner screen

Both options stand out clearly from recent iPhone screens.

The outer screen will be considerably smaller than what we're used to, while the inner screen will be larger than that of the iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The iPhone Ultra's body will be shorter than other modern iPhones, but at the same time wider. Compared with past iPhones, this could result in a rather distinctive look and feel.

How iOS and apps will adapt to the new screen format and size, we won't know until September.

That said, judging from the current iOS 27 beta, Apple is working on enabling landscape mode support for iPhone apps. Third-party apps are expected to follow suit, taking full advantage of that inner screen, which is even larger than the iPad mini's.

What are your thoughts on the rumored design of the iPhone Ultra? Let us know in the comments section.
